issues.explanation: 'Heavy make-up' is hard to reconcile with this patient's demographics (22-year-old single male auditor) and the rest of the profile unless there is a specific unreported context such as concealment or gender expression. In this profile it stands out as clinically implausible relative to the other items, whereas the other maladaptive strategies center on vigilance, escape, and social evaluation.

vignette: Clinical Vignette for Amir Amir, a 22-year-old Middle Eastern male auditor, sought help after experiencing intense distress and anxiety following a traumatic incident of rape. The event occurred during his college years when he was home visiting family in the summer. On a hot afternoon, he accepted an invitation from an acquaintance to have coffee at their apartment complex, only to be violently attacked while inside. Since that day, Amir has been haunted by certain triggers and maladaptive strategies that have significantly impacted his daily life. The smell of strong cologne or perfume often transports him back to the moment when the attacker was nearby, causing a surge of panic and hypervigilance. Additionally, encounters with people misbehaving in public spaces, such as yelling or arguing loudly, evoke vivid memories of the attack's chaotic atmosphere. Amir had come to believe that his ex-partner's comments about past relationships were reminiscent of the assault, particularly when they mentioned anything related to trust and betrayal. These reminders deeply upset him, making it difficult for him to engage in any meaningful interactions with former partners or even think about future relationships without feeling overwhelmed by a sense of loss and humiliation. In response to these triggers, Amir has adopted several maladaptive strategies that have become habitual over time. He now makes sure to always stay close to the exit when he is in unfamiliar places, often choosing to sit near doors during meetings at work or social gatherings with friends. This behavior stems from a deep-seated belief that he needs to be able to leave quickly if danger arises, which has made it challenging for him to fully engage in his role as an auditor where networking and attending conferences are essential. Amir also avoids situations where he feels like others will evaluate him-whether it's his appearance or performance. For instance, he has started wearing concealing clothing that makes him feel less visible and thus safer. This change in wardrobe is not only a physical coping mechanism but also reflects his underlying fear of being noticed and potentially vulnerable again. His body remains constantly tense, always ready to react to danger, which manifests as persistent muscle tightness and an ongoing sense of alertness. Any sudden movement by others immediately puts him on guard, leading to constant scanning of his surroundings for potential threats. This heightened state of vigilance has made it difficult for Amir to relax or enjoy leisure activities. Moreover, Amir has internalized a negative appraisal that he feels someone else would not have gotten into this situation; this belief fuels his self-doubt and feelings of being permanently humiliated by what happened. He laments the loss of happiness he used to feel, often reflecting on how different life was before the attack, now filled with constant misery. These thoughts and behaviors have strained Amir's relationships at work and socially. His colleagues have noticed a change in his demeanor and approach to teamwork, leading to less collaboration and more isolation. He has also begun to avoid social outings with friends for fear of encountering any triggers that could set off another episode of intense anxiety or flashbacks. What finally brought Amir to seek help was the realization that these symptoms were not only affecting his mental health but also his career and personal life. The cumulative impact of avoiding situations, feeling constantly on edge, and experiencing a profound sense of humiliation had become too overwhelming. He is most afraid of never being able to trust anyone again or fully reclaim his life from the trauma. However, Amir is also hoping for relief from these debilitating symptoms and support in rebuilding his confidence and happiness. Through therapy, he aims to process the traumatic event, challenge negative appraisals, and develop healthier coping strategies that will allow him to live a more fulfilling and less constrained life.
